payload.question: Is the council borrowing more than it is allowed to?
payload.label: Borrowing against the limits full Council set, 2025/26
payload.council_caveat: The £145.948m is the council's own estimate, not an audited outturn: every column of the table it comes from, in the 2026/27 treasury strategy, is headed "Estimate", and the same table restates the 2025/26 limits rather than reproducing the strategy full Council approved that year. The council is heavily under-borrowed — it uses its own cash instead of taking loans. That changes in 2026/27, when the strategy plans about £42m of new external borrowing, taking gross debt to £188.6m.
payload.evidence: Full Council sets two lines on its own borrowing every year. The operational boundary is the level it expects to work within — £314.409m for 2025/26 — and the authorised limit is the legal ceiling it may not pass, £344.409m. Against them the council puts its external borrowing at £145.948m, well inside both. Nearly all of it is Public Works Loan Board money, government lending at government rates. Borrowing far below a ceiling is not by itself good or bad: the ceiling is a limit, not something to aim at.

ai.reviewed_by: two independent AI review passes, reconciled against the source documents, 8 September 2026
